text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe announced yesterday he would resign whether the right-wing coalition wins the second round of the parliamentary election or not. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation, The IHT).
LES ECHOS
-- European federation of labour unions calls for a demonstration on May 28 for European labour and employment.
-- CDR company set up to sell off Credit Lyonnais assets sells 80 percent of its stake in Total for 1.9 billion francs.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Supermarkets group Cora to ally with British and Dutch retailer in the Europartner buying group, in which competitor Carrefour holds a 42.4 stake.
-- Minority shareholders question terms of joint venture between Vallourec and Mannesmann.
-- Ameritech U.S.-based telephone operator chairman Walter Catlow in an interview says does not rule out developing activities in France, notably in the Internet transactions market.
L'AGEFI
-- Operators on the Paris markets remain relatively calm in spaite of the unexpected leadership of the opposition left in the first round of the parliamentary election.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Activity at companies which place temporary workers rose by some 13 percent in a year.
-- Axa-UAP sold some seven billion francs worth of assets since the beginning of 1997 with an estimated 700-million-franc capital gain.
-- Time Warner considers buying 35 percent of the CGV and 10 percent of CanalSatellite digital-TV channel. Canal Plus would retain subscriber management operations for CGV.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- National credit council calls for reform of French law to follow boom of transactions on the Internet.
-- Workers at Renault Vilvoorde plant to hold referendum on possible layoff plan.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- The euro and president Jacques Chirac seen as the big losers in the parliamentary election.
-- French stocks tumble on Socialists showing.
